headline: Building a brand's online presence from scratch
tldr: A trusted, family-run saree store in Hyderabad had no online presence at all. Alongside my full-time design role, I built it from zero: brand identity, AI-powered content, a constant stream of Reels and Shorts, and a website. In two months: 95 posts and Shorts across Instagram and YouTube, and 3.2K+ Instagram views a month.

segments.text: Alongside my full-time work as a UI/UX designer, I started a side hustle 2 months ago: building the online presence of
Divya Silks
, a family-run saree and handloom store in Uppal, Hyderabad, trusted since 2003. There was no existing digital presence, no brand system, and no content, so I built everything from scratch.
My goal:
grow online reach and turn views into real enquiries and sales.
My role:
solo, end-to-end owner. Brand strategist, social media manager, content creator, video editor, graphic designer, web designer, and growth marketer.
Strong offline trust, built over two decades, but none of it was visible online.

items.text: Zero digital visibility
despite a loyal offline customer base
Starting from nothing:
no brand identity, no content, no website
No way to browse:
customers could not see the collection online
No system
for content, posting, or measuring results
Limited budget,
so every effort had to be organic and resourceful
Limited time:
managing it all alongside a full-time role

segments.text: Nine workstreams, run by one person. Each one closes a gap between a customer scrolling Instagram and a customer walking into the store.

Explored several logo directions before finalising the mark, then created a consistent visual language: logo usage, watermarking on every post, and a premium, warm aesthetic suited to silk and handloom products.
Planned a consistent posting calendar focused on short-form saree videos showcasing drape, texture, and craft, published as Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts.
Used
Higgsfield
for AI-generated visuals and video, and
ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude
for captions, content ideas, and marketing copy. This let me produce high-quality content quickly as a one-person team.
Constantly shooting new sarees in store and editing them into Shorts and Reels in
VN Video Editor, Edits, and CapCut
, with a consistent look, background, framing, and watermark to build a recognisable feed.
Posted Instagram Stories daily to stay visible and drive engagement. Organised Story Highlights by collection (Ajrak, Banarasi, Jamdani, and more) so customers can browse like a catalogue.
Designed promotional posters for collections, offers, and festive seasons.
Partnered with creators and other accounts to reach new audiences.
Rewrote the bio with a clear category, a trust signal ("Trusted Since 2003"), the store location, and links to YouTube and Threads.
Designed and built a website from scratch using
Claude and VS Code
so customers can explore the collection and contact the store, creating a path from social media to purchase.

Before landing on the final loom-and-charkha mark, I explored six directions, from elephant motifs to a temple-and-paisley crest, a weaving-shuttle monogram, a flowing saree, and a minimal thread-spool mark. I tested how each one felt at profile-picture size and as a watermark.
The final mark

turns the "D" of Divya into a handloom: a loom frame, a charkha, and a flowing saree border, in gold on deep navy. It reads as heritage and craft at a glance, holds up as a small profile picture, and works as a watermark on every post.
Festive greetings keep the store present during peak saree-buying seasons, and event posters drive footfall. Every poster carries the logo, the store address, and the same warm, premium look.

segments.text: Showing up daily built visibility faster than occasional polished posts.

items.text: AI is a force multiplier.
AI tools turned a one-person side hustle into a full content and marketing team.
Trust is the story.
A traditional business's biggest asset online is its story and trust, so I put "since 2003" front and centre.
Design drives outcomes.
Wearing every hat (designer, marketer, editor, strategist, builder) showed me how design decisions directly affect business results.
Always learning.
I keep picking up new marketing and growth techniques and applying them in real time.
